notes: Rice Lake digital weight indicators. Default serial output is continuous mode.
Rice Lake indicators via TCP/IP Ethernet option.

Avery Weigh-Tronix ZM-301 and ZM series indicators. Uses SMA 8.1.2 protocol over TCP. Response may include command echo ('W') or space before status byte. Parser should locate header by pattern: [status][digit][G/N/T]. Default port 10001 via serial-to-Ethernet converter.
Avery Weigh-Tronix ZM series via RS-232 serial. Same SMA protocol as TCP variant. Check parity setting on your unit (default Even, 7 data bits).
Mettler Toledo industrial terminals. Default parity is Odd — verify on your unit.
Digi-Star livestock and truck scale indicators.

responseFormat: SMA 8.1.2: LF + [echo/pad] + status + range + gross/net + motion + future + weight + unit + CR
notes: Generic SMA 8.1.2 demand-mode protocol. Send 'W' to request weight. Response includes binary status byte, range, gross/net, motion flags. Parser should find header by pattern [status][digit][G/N/T] to handle optional command echo.
Generic continuous-output scale. Adjust regex to match your scale's output format.
Generic SMA 8.1.2 demand protocol over TCP/IP. Send 'W' to request weight. Common default port is 10001 via serial-to-Ethernet converter.

Cardinal 225 on-demand serial format. Service sends 'Gross\r'; scale replies with LF + status + range + mode (G/T/N) + motion + custom + signed weight (xxxxxx.xxx) + units + CR. Status: Z=center of zero, O=over capacity, E=zero error, e=weight not displayed. Default 9600,8,N,1.

Cardinal 225 Navigator continuous serial stream in IQ355 format. Each frame is right-justified weight + unit (LB/KG) + mode (G/N/T) + optional motion flag 'MO'. Default 9600,8,N,1. Set ConnectionType=Serial and Protocol=IQ355 on the scale config. SerialPortName examples: 'COM1' (Windows), '/dev/ttyUSB0' (Linux).

responseFormat: <STX><POL><wwwwwww><UNIT><G/N><S><TERM>  per Rice Lake IQ plus 355 EDP/PRN stream; STX often suppressed in serial captures
notes: Rice Lake IQ plus 355 EDP/PRN continuous output stream — also used by Condec UMC indicators (e.g. UMC600 series) and other relabels of the same OEM board. Each frame is <STX><POL><wwwwwww><UNIT><G/N><S><TERM>, where POL is one of "<SP>" (positive), "-" (negative), "^" (overload, weight = ^^^^^^^), "]" (underrange, weight = ]]]]]]]); wwwwwww is 7-digit right-justified weight with leading-space suppression; UNIT is L=lb, K=kg, T=ton, G=g, O=oz, SP=none; G/N is G=gross, N=net, T=tare; S is SP=valid, I=invalid, M=motion, O=over/under range; TERM is CR or CRLF. Regex captures: (1) signed weight, (2) unit char, (3) mode char, (4) status char (used to surface motion to the operator). STX (0x02) at frame start is optional in practice — some firmware or USB-serial converters strip it before delivery. Default 9600,8,N,1; a few older Condec models default to 7,E,1. Set STREAM=EDP or STREAM=PRN in the indicator's SERIAL menu.

Mettler Toledo IND700 (and IND560 / IND570 / IND780) terminals via the Shared Data Server, TCP 1701. The service logs in with the terminal user/password set on the scale (user <name> -> 12 Access OK or 51 Enter Password; pass <password>), keeps the session open and polls wt0101 (displayed gross weight) and wt0103 (units) every poll interval. Zero writes wc0104=1 (pushbutton zero), which needs a user with Operator write access or above. The IND700 Shared Data Reference does not document motion / center-of-zero / over-capacity fields; if your terminal has them, add motion / centerOfZero / overCapacity / underZero to sdsFields (read as 1 = active). A non-numeric gross (dashes when over/under range) is reported as Error. Field instance 01 = scale 1; use wt0201 etc. for scale 2.
